meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Common Levantine word (from Italian arma) for a shopfront sign.

examples.trans: The shop has a big sign outside.
I saw the blue sign above the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with the speaker's gender: a man says أنا آسف, a woman says أنا آسفة.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for the delay.
Sorry for the bother, sir.

meanings.note: Describes a place or thing that is safe; for people 'safe and sound' is سالم.

examples.trans: The neighbourhood here is safe at night.
These stairs are not safe for children.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Exclamation when a puzzle clicks into place ('aha!').

examples.trans: Aha! Now I understand the whole story!
Aha, that is why you took the bus!

meanings.note: Reinforces negation ('not at all, never'): ما في زبدة أبدا ('no butter at all'), لا تقلق أبدا ('do not worry at all').

examples.trans: There is no butter in the fridge at all!
Do not worry at all, sir.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأجر, بيأجر).

examples.trans: We do not usually rent out the attic.
We rented out all the rooms this week.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of منيح ('good'). Before a noun without ال- it means 'the best' (أحسن نومة 'the best sleep').

examples.trans: This is the best room in the house.
I feel better today.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of حلو ('sweet, lovely').

examples.trans: It has the loveliest view of the courtyard.
This is the nicest day of the week.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday adverb 'sometimes'.

examples.trans: Sometimes air gets into the pipes at night.
Sometimes we have tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of دافي ('warm'); also spelled أدفا.

examples.trans: The piano's sound is warmer when it rains.
The attic is the warmest room in winter.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fourteen'.

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
It is seven fourteen.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Collective noun for cedar wood or cedar trees.

examples.trans: This is an old cedar wood box.
The scent of cedar wood is very pleasant.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite having no -a ending; means ground, land, or indoor floor.

examples.trans: The floor is clean and dry now.
Set the box on the floor for a moment.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أرضية, plural: أرضيين).

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the ground floor.
The ground-floor rooms are close to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أرضيات.

examples.trans: The floorboards are old and sturdy.
We wiped the floor in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بزعج, بيزعج).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
Sorry if we disturbed you at night.

meanings.note: In everyday Amman speech, أزمة most often means heavy city traffic.

examples.trans: Downtown traffic at noon is slow.
We arrived ten minutes before the traffic jam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of سيئ ('bad').

examples.trans: The news is worse than we expected.
This is the worst time for rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

أصلا.gloss: anyway; in the first place; actually

meanings.en: anyway; in the first place; actually
meanings.note: Everyday conversational adverb meaning 'in the first place / anyway / to begin with'.

examples.trans: Does the attic even have a comfortable bed?
The wire needed adjusting anyway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أصلية, plural: أصليين).

examples.trans: The ceiling is solid oak wood.
All the old tilework is original.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of طويل ('tall, long').

examples.trans: You have grown taller than the piano!
The bridge route is two minutes longer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of غريب ('strange').

examples.trans: The story gets stranger every hour.
That is the strangest request I have heard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective.

examples.trans: Guests wake up early for the most part.
Most houses here are made of stone.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; the plural أغاني (aghaani) is the one you hear most.

examples.trans: This is an old song my grandmother loves.
We listen to songs in the car every morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective.

examples.trans: At least the bread is ready in the oven.
We need less than ten minutes.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of أكثر ('more, most').

examples.trans: I liked working here much more.
Who knows the neighbourhood better than you?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باكل, بياكل).

examples.trans: The brothers are eating lemon cake in the courtyard.
We ate a hot breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Means 'certainly, definitely' or 'must be' (إنتي أكيد نور 'you must be Nour').

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

ألقى.gloss: to cast; take (ألقي نظرة take a look)

meanings.en: to cast; take (ألقي نظرة take a look)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلقي, بيلقي).

examples.trans: Let me take a look at the letter.
He took a quick look at the ledger.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian way to answer or check a phone line.

examples.trans: Hello? Jasmine House, how may I help you?
Hello, can you hear me clearly?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Safety in the house is very important.
They arrived safely and securely.

meanings.note: Means something kept in trust for someone, and in Amman also names City Hall (أمانة عمان).

examples.trans: I have something entrusted for you from your grandfather.
We put the bag in the left-luggage closet.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أنوف.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your nose now.
The air feels cold on my nose in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقذ, بينقذ).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
You saved my whole trip.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of هادي ('quiet, calm').

examples.trans: Jasmine House is the calmest place in Amman.
The street is much quieter at night.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: Lighthearted exclamation after a small spill or slip.

examples.trans: Oops! A drop of juice landed on my tie!
Oops, I left the pen on the desk.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Jordan, Syria, Lebanon and Palestine use the old Syriac-derived month names: كانون التاني January ... أيار May ... أيلول September.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'when?'.

examples.trans: When does the hardware shop open?
When did the bus arrive at the station?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أباريق.

examples.trans: The teapot is hot on the table.
Pour the hot water into the teapot.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Used constantly in the polite phrase عن إذنك ('excuse me / with your permission').

examples.trans: Excuse me, may I pass?
He asked permission before heading out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for the disturbance.
There is no bother at all.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: إشعارات.

examples.trans: An official notice arrived in the mail.
I read the notice twice.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: إطلالات.

examples.trans: The room has a lovely view onto the courtyard.
This is the prettiest view in the house.

meanings.note: Means 'except / unless' (إلا إذا 'unless') and 'minutes to the hour' (اطنعش إلا خمسة 'five to twelve').

examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve!

examples.text: ما حدا بيقيس الساحة إلا مهندس!
examples.trans: Nobody measures a courtyard except an engineer!

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one man.

examples.trans: Did you plant these herbs yourself?
Did you plan this entire meeting?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: Carries the direct object pronoun after بدي ('want'): هاد اللي بدي إياه ('that is what I want').

examples.trans: That is exactly what I want.
I gave it to you this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: إيجارات.

examples.trans: The shop rent is paid until summer.
We signed the lease today.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببتسم, بيبتسم).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
He smiled when he saw his brother.

meanings.note: Combines with عم ('paternal uncle') as ابن عمي ('my cousin').

examples.text: ابن عمي ساكن قريب من هون.
examples.trans: My cousin lives near here.
The boys are playing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصل, بيتصل).

examples.trans: Call the lost-and-found office right away.
You called us on Tuesday.

meanings.note: Said on its own, اتفقنا ('we agreed') is the everyday way to close a deal: 'deal!'.

examples.text: اتفقنا، بنلتقي الساعة تسعة عند الباب.
examples.trans: Agreed, we meet at nine at the door.

examples.text: اتفقت مع سلمى على كيكة الجمعة.
examples.trans: I agreed with Salma about the Friday cake.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian for 12. From eleven up, the counted noun stays singular: اتنعش فنجان 'twelve cups'.

examples.trans: We have twelve guests tonight.
It's twelve noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحتاج, بيحتاج).

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.
An old house needs steady care.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحترم, بيحترم).

examples.trans: We respect the Amman tourist guide!
Everyone respects Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Often placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'spare' (مفتاح احتياط a spare key).

examples.trans: I have a spare key in the drawer.
We bought a spare valve for winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بختار, بيختار).

examples.trans: I chose this quarter for a family reason.
They chose a table under the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: اختيارات.

examples.trans: A wonderful choice for breakfast!
That was our choice from the start.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتاح, بيرتاح).

examples.trans: Rest up after your journey, ma'am.
We rested in the courtyard with a glass of tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتبك, بيرتبك).

examples.trans: I got flustered and rang the doorbell.
Do not get flustered; take your time speaking.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستاهل, بيستاهل).

examples.trans: Your welcome deserves ten out of ten!
The house is worth all this effort.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستعجل, بيستعجل).

examples.trans: Hurry, the guests are coming down the stairs!
Do not rush to go upstairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستعمل, بيستعمل).

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
I used the last valve in winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستقبل, بيستقبل).

examples.trans: Let us go down to welcome the new guest.
They welcomed us with a smile and hot tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتاق, بيشتاق).

examples.trans: I missed you so much over these three years.
We missed our Friday gatherings.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتري, بيشتري).

examples.trans: Tell me exactly what to buy.
Buy both brass valves together.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتغل, بيشتغل).

examples.trans: Look, the flame came on blue!
He works on heritage buildings in Amman.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعتذر, بيعتذر).

examples.trans: I must apologize to you frankly.
He apologized for the mistake on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعتمد, بيعتمد).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We rely on Nour at reception.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He called us on Tuesday.
The corner shop is open every Tuesday.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمع.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتهي, بينتهي).

examples.trans: The problem ended well.
We thought everything was over.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسحب, بينسحب).

examples.trans: I shall retreat to my office with dignity!
He quietly stepped out of the room.

meanings.note: The n-pattern of فتح: the thing opens by itself, nobody is named (الباب انفتح 'the door came open').

examples.trans: The window blew open by itself in the wind.
The old lock does not open easily.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنكتب, بينكتب).

examples.trans: Your name will be written in the big ledger!
The address was written in clear handwriting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنكسر, بينكسر).

examples.trans: The brass pressure valve broke.
Not a single glass broke in the kitchen.

اهتم.gloss: to take care of; look after

meanings.en: to take care of; look after
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهتم, بيهتم).

examples.trans: Someone has to look after the courtyard plants.
They looked after the guests like family.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: باردة, plural: باردين).

examples.trans: Here, drink a glass of cold water.
My hands were cold from the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببيع, بيبيع).

examples.trans: The hardware shop sells this size.
I thought it was lost when we sold the house!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواقي.

examples.trans: Here you go, here is five dinars change.
I counted the change on the table.

meanings.note: Used in core Jordanian idioms like طول بالك ('be patient'), هدي بالك ('calm down'), and جاي على بالي ('I feel like').

examples.trans: Be patient a moment, everything is fine.

examples.text: جاي على بالي كاسة شاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: I feel like having a glass of mint tea.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Jordanian and Levantine 'for free', built from ب + بلاش ('with nothing').

examples.trans: Tea is free with breakfast.
I got the chair for free from the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بجعات.

examples.trans: We saw a white swan on the water.
The drawing of the swan is very pretty.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببدا, بيبدا).

examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.
The day began lively and bright.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Preposition 'without'; followed by ما + verb it means 'without -ing' (بدون ما ياخد 'without taking').

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: برتقالات.

examples.trans: The fresh orange juice is cold.
We bought oranges and apples from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أبراج.

examples.trans: The downtown clock tower is old.
We heard the tower bell at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببرد, بيبرد).

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the rack right now.
The radiator is starting to get cold at the bottom.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word (from Turkish burgu) for a metal screw.

examples.trans: I tightened the screw with the small screwdriver.
The chair needs a new screw.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A postcard arrived in the morning.
The postman rang the bell.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بسطات.

examples.trans: Turn left at the stair landing.
The landing is wide and bright.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بطاقات.

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.

examples.trans: Take off your heavy coat and sit down.
He took off his wet shoes by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشم, بيشم).

examples.trans: Smell that wonderful aroma in the kitchen!
We smelled the cinnamon from the stairs.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite no -a ending.

examples.trans: The warm sun came out after the rain.
Read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شهور.

examples.trans: That was the best sleep in a month!
The contract renews at the start of next month.

meanings.note: Relational adjective built from شهر ('month') with -ي.

examples.trans: We pay a fixed monthly rent.
They earn a good monthly salary.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شوربات.

examples.trans: Here is a cup of hot vegetable soup.
Hot soup is wonderful on a rainy day.

شوي.gloss: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)

meanings.en: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)
meanings.note: Means 'a bit / a moment' (استنوا شوي 'wait a moment'); doubled شوي شوي means 'slowly, gently'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Construct form of شوي used directly before a noun: شوية زبدة ('a little butter'), شوية هوا ('a bit of air').

examples.text: بس شوية زبدة مع الخبز، شكرا.
examples.trans: Just a little butter with the bread, thank you.
A little air gets into it at night.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

examples.trans: Everything is ready on the table.

examples.text: رن الجرس إذا احتجت أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Levantine word for slatted window shutters, used as a collective: الشيش مسكر 'the shutters are closed'.

examples.trans: Close the shutters, the sun is strong.
Green shutters suit the house.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشبك, بيشبك).

examples.trans: Plug in Tariq's brass lamp.
We clipped the second sheet to the envelope.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: There is clean soap and a towel in the bathroom.
The scent of olive soap is natural.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صادقة, plural: صادقين).

examples.trans: A short, sincere sentence from the heart.
Be honest with your brother.

صار.gloss: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)

meanings.en: to become; happen; be alright (ما بصير must not)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصب, بيصب).

examples.text: صبي المي السخنة بالإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Pour the hot water into the pot, Nour.
Allow me to pour the orange juice.

meanings.note: Used in the universal morning greeting صباح الخير ('good morning'), answered with صباح النور.

examples.trans: Good morning! How did you sleep today?
The weather is very pleasant this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صباحية, plural: صباحيين).

examples.trans: We opened a morning café for the neighbours.
I love morning coffee in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your patience with us.
Patience is the key to relief.

صبّح.gloss: to wake in the morning (تصبح على خير good night)

meanings.en: to wake in the morning (تصبح على خير good night)
meanings.note: Subjunctive تصبح على خير (to a man) / تصبحي على خير (to a woman) is the standard Jordanian 'good night' ('may you wake to goodness').

examples.trans: Good night, sir!
Good night, see you at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday word confirming something is right ('right! / true!').

examples.text: صح! في صفحة تانية ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: Right! There is a second page behind the letter.
What you say is completely true.

meanings.note: Its dual صحتين ('two healths!', often صحتين وهنا) is Jordan's warmest 'enjoy your meal/tea!'.

examples.trans: Enjoy your breakfast!
The most important thing in life is health.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصحى, بيصحى).

examples.trans: Room four wakes up at quarter past seven.
I woke up early to the birdsong.

meanings.note: Transitive, with a doubled h (sahha): you wake someone else. Compare صحي, to wake up yourself.

examples.trans: Wake me up at six, please.
The bell woke all the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صدف.

examples.trans: What a sweet coincidence!
We met at the market by chance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Thank you for telling the truth.
Honesty builds trust between people.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صدمات.

examples.trans: My hands went cold from the shock.
The plan was a surprise, not a shock.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصداء.

examples.trans: Wood softens the echo in the room.
We heard the echo of the voice in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used constantly as بصراحة or bare صراحة ('honestly / to be frank').

examples.trans: Honestly, I loved the place very much.
Frankly, the coffee here is excellent.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصرخ, بيصرخ).

examples.trans: Tell me, did he yell or was he calm?

examples.text: ما حدا صرخ، الكل تفهم الوضع.
examples.trans: Nobody yelled; everyone understood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صريحة, plural: صريحين).

examples.trans: Let us be candid from the start.
A frank and clear answer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صعبة, plural: صعبين).

examples.trans: Family disagreements are always hard.

examples.text: الزبدة المالحة صعبة مع المربى الحلو.
examples.trans: Salted butter is tricky with sweet jam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صفوف.

examples.trans: We sat in the front row at the concert.
The chairs are arranged in two rows.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: Clap your hands, or clap for a performer at the end.

examples.trans: People clapped a lot after the song.
Clap twice and the lamp lights up.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصلح, بيصلح).

examples.trans: I fix pipes and chairs.
Yesterday you fixed the old heater.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صمامات.

examples.trans: We fitted a new brass valve on the boiler.
Make sure the valve is tightly shut.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصمم, بيصمم).

examples.trans: Do you design concert and music halls?
He designed a quiet courtyard in the city centre.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صوتيات.

examples.trans: He works as an architectural acoustics engineer.
The acoustics of the old hall are excellent.

meanings.note: Any picture or photograph; صورة أبيض وأسود is a black-and-white photo.

examples.trans: I took a nice photo of you in the courtyard.
I have old photos of my grandmother.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصواف.

examples.trans: This wool sweater is warm and soft.
A wool blanket is cosy in winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The item is safe and sound with us.
The letter arrived safe and sound.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Regular maintenance protects the building.
We called the maintenance technician in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صيدليات.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is beside the overpass.
I walked past the pharmacy this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضيع, بيضيع).

examples.text: فكرت القطار ضاع لما بعنا البيت!
examples.trans: I thought the train got lost when we sold the house!
You will not get lost; the road is straight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضايق, بيضايق).

examples.trans: Do the extra stairs not bother you?
Sorry if we bothered you with the noise.

meanings.note: Active participle of ضل ('to remain'); standard Jordanian for 'there is ... left'.

examples.trans: He has two valves left on the shelf.
How much time is left until noon?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضبط, بيضبط).

examples.trans: Set the alarm for six, Tariq.
The plan worked out one hundred percent!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Outside on the main street there is noise.
Thick stone blocks traffic noise.

ضرب.gloss: to hit; strike; (of a fuse) blow

meanings.en: to hit; strike; (of a fuse) blow
meanings.note: Basic meaning 'to hit'. In everyday Jordanian a fuse or a machine 'hits' when it blows or fails (الفيوز ضرب 'the fuse blew').

examples.trans: The ball hit the window.

examples.text: الفيوز ضرب لما شغلنا الفرن والغسالة مع بعض.
examples.trans: The fuse blew when we ran the oven and the washing machine together.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أضعاف.

examples.trans: Today we baked double the usual amount.
The courtyard holds twice this number.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضغوط.

examples.trans: The pressure valve on the boiler works.
Calm tea eases blood pressure.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضواو.

examples.trans: The yellow light beside the bed is warm.
Turn on the light in the hallway, please.

ضوّى.gloss: to light up; shine; switch on a light

meanings.en: to light up; shine; switch on a light
meanings.note: Used for a lamp that glows and for the person who switches it on (ضوي الضو 'turn on the light').

examples.trans: The new lamp gives good light.
Turn the light on, the room is dark.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: You have a real gift for hospitality!
Warm hospitality opens hearts.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ضيقة, plural: ضيقين).

examples.trans: The attic stairs are a bit narrow.
Do not enter the narrow alley.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضيع, بيضيع).

examples.text: الورق ما بيضيع أسماء الغرف وقت المطر.
examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names when it rains.
Mazen always misplaces his glasses!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طازجة, plural: طازجين).

examples.trans: Morning bread is fresh and hot!
Fresh orange juice and fresh cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Warm, reassuring 'of course! / naturally!'.

examples.trans: Of course, Tariq, your secret is safe with us!
Of course I came when I got your card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طبيعية, plural: طبيعيين).

examples.trans: Great service is a natural thing at our inn.
Natural juice without sugar.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أطراف.

examples.trans: Pull the edge of the sheet tight.

examples.text: حط الكاسة بعيد عن طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Set the glass away from the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Used in عالطريق ('on the way') and طول الطريق ('all the way').

examples.trans: The hot tea is on the way right now!
I repeated the sentence all along the way.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طرق.

examples.trans: We made the eggs the French way.
This is an easy, quick method.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طعوم.

examples.trans: The exact same delicious taste!
The fresh lemon flavour stands out in the cake.

meanings.note: A light or fire goes out (الضو طفى 'the light went out'); with a person as subject, to switch something off.

examples.trans: The power went out for a whole hour.
Switch off the light before you sleep.

meanings.note: Sound word for a sharp noise: a click, a pop or a crack.

examples.trans: I heard a pop from the kitchen.
Crack! The glass broke.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The weather in Amman is mild in spring.
I looked out the window to check the weather.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلب, بيطلب).

examples.trans: The postman just asked for my signature.

examples.text: طلبت منه يقابلك هون يوم الجمعة؟
examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here on Friday?

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: To paint a wall, door or shutter with a brush; the paint itself is دهان.

examples.trans: We painted the door blue last year.
We want to paint the children's room yellow.

meanings.note: Form II طلّع means both 'look!' (طلّع بالمراية) and 'bring/carry up' (رح أطلّع الشنتة).

examples.text: طلع بالمراية ورا المكتب يا معلم!
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk, boss!
I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

طمّن.gloss: to reassure; tell how things went

meanings.en: to reassure; tell how things went
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطمن, بيطمن).

examples.trans: Tell me, how did the room go?
He put our minds at ease with a kind word.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طوارئ.

examples.trans: We have a small emergency in the kitchen!
The emergency key hangs beside the door.

meanings.note: Collective noun for bricks or building blocks; حيط طوب is a brick wall.

examples.trans: The house is built of brick and stone.
They brought new bricks for the wall.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطوي, بيطوي).

examples.trans: Fold this sheet and put it in your pocket.
She folded the clean towels in the closet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طويلة, plural: طوال).

examples.text: في رجال طويل واقف عند البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a tall man standing by the gate.
Three years was a long time.

طوّل.gloss: to take long; be patient (طول بالك take it easy)

meanings.en: to be patient (طول بالك take it easy)
meanings.note: طوّل بالك ('lengthen your patience' = take it easy, hold on!) is a classic Levantine expression.

examples.text: طول بالك يا أستاذ، اقرأ الصفحة التانية!
examples.trans: Hold on, sir, read the second page!
I did not take long at the market; I came right back.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطل, بيطل).

examples.text: مازن بيطل من ورا الستارة كل دقيقة!
examples.trans: Mazen peeks from behind the curtain every minute!
The window overlooks the courtyard and the tree.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عائلية, plural: عائليين).

examples.trans: I came to the neighbourhood for an old family reason.
This is a quiet family hotel.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعيد, بيعيد).

examples.trans: I will repeat the words the whole way!
Could you repeat the number, please?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عادات.

examples.trans: Usually we open the gate at seven.
Drinking morning coffee is a nice habit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عادية, plural: عاديين).

examples.trans: Bread with jam needs regular unsalted butter.
A quiet, ordinary day in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعيش, بيعيش).

examples.trans: This house has lived through eighty winters!
They lived in our quarter for many years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عواطف.

examples.trans: Good maintenance has nothing sentimental about it!
He spoke with his brother with genuine warmth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عاقلة, plural: عاقلين).

examples.text: ما في حدا عاقل بيرفض خبز سخن!
examples.trans: No sensible person turns down hot bread!
Sensible, measured words.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عالقة, plural: عالقين).

examples.text: فتحتي بابنا العالق من أول يوم!
examples.trans: You opened our sticking door on day one!
The key was stuck in the lock.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عالية, plural: عاليين).

examples.trans: What is that loud sound upstairs?
The wooden ceiling is high and sunny.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عامة, plural: عامين).

examples.text: عالشارع العام برا في ضجة سيارات.
examples.trans: Out on the main road there is traffic noise.
A public park near the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عمال.

examples.trans: The movers carried out the furniture in the morning.
Every worker in the bakery knows his job.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعبر, بيعبر).

examples.trans: Cross the overpass to downtown.
We crossed the street at the light.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عتبات.

examples.trans: We found the suitcase on the doorstep.
We swept the stone threshold in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عجلات.

examples.trans: Turn the blue valve wheel slowly.

examples.text: القطار الصغير إله أربع عجلات خشب.
examples.trans: The little train has four wooden wheels.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عجين.

examples.trans: The bread dough is ready in the oven.
She left the dough to rest half an hour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عدد.

examples.trans: The screwdriver and wrench are in the toolbox.
He brought the tools to fix the boiler.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عروض.

examples.trans: He measured the width of the courtyard.
The ring is twenty millimetres wide.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعرف, بيعرف).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting in two seconds!
Do you know anyone here in Amman?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عريضة, plural: عراض).

examples.trans: The wide desk under the window is comfortable.
There are wide wooden beams in the ceiling.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Piano playing calms the nerves.
Whenever she finishes playing, she smiles.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: We booked a table for dinner tomorrow evening.
Dinner is ready at eight o'clock.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أعشاب.

examples.trans: We sprinkled green herbs on top of the eggs.
Tariq grows fresh herbs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصافير.

examples.trans: We hear the birds in the tree.
We set out water for the birds in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصاير.

examples.trans: Fresh orange juice is cold and tasty.
I poured two glasses of juice for breakfast.

meanings.note: Any time off work or school; in Jordan the weekly break is Friday and Saturday.

examples.trans: Next holiday we are going to Aqaba.
Tomorrow is a day off, there is no work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عظيمة, plural: عظيمين).

examples.text: شوربة سخنة بالمطر؟ هاد شي عظيم!
examples.trans: Hot soup in the rain? That is splendid!
A great idea, everyone.

meanings.note: Jordanian everyday word for furniture and all your belongings when you move house.

examples.trans: We moved the furniture in a big truck.
The living-room furniture is old but comfortable.

meanings.note: Used both to get someone's attention politely ('excuse me') and to reply to شكرا ('you're welcome').

examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?
Excuse me, Mr. Rami, sorry for the bother.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عقارات.

examples.trans: The letter came from the property department.
Property prices downtown are high.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عقود.

examples.trans: The lease contract is protected by law.
He works at the municipal contracts office.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علامات.

examples.trans: He got a score of ten out of ten.
There is a small mark on the wood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علب.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
I saved this old wooden box.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علالي.

examples.trans: The attic room on the third floor is sunny.
We brought the boxes down from the attic.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

What you say is one hundred percent right.

We cleaned the washbasin and mirror in the morning.

The inspector checked the building's safety features.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفتوحة, plural: مفتوحين).

Here is to neighbours and our open gates!

The brass hinges of the chest are intact.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مفقودات.

He handed the wallet in to lost property.

Pass me the screwdriver from the toolbox.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفكرة, plural: مفكرين).

I thought the shop was closed today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مقابلة, plural: —).

The pharmacy is in the building across the way.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مقاسات.

examples.trans: This size fits you perfectly.
The shop sells all pipe sizes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مقلية, plural: مقليين).

examples.trans: Fried eggs with herbs are delicious.
Hot, crispy fried potatoes.

She finished the call in two minutes.

Everything is tidy in its proper place.

The wooden desk under the window is wide.

The public library is a quiet place to read.

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

examples.trans: Put the broken valve in your coat pocket.
We fixed the broken chair leg.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ملاحظات.

Thank you for that helpful observation.

examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
I cannot find the key in my pocket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ملزقة, plural: ملزقين).

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the handle.
The key was taped underneath the box.

examples.text: حطي معلقة صغيرة جنب كل فنجان.
examples.trans: Put a small spoon beside every cup.
The silver spoons are in the top drawer.

The parcel is wrapped with great care.

He measured the part to the millimetre.

The shower water was hot and excellent!

examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
The hallway is dark, turn on the light.

examples.trans: It was a cold, rainy day.
Winter this year is very rainy.

examples.trans: May I see the room first?
Could I see the tag in the sunlight?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مملة, plural: مملين).

We thought it was a dull municipal notice.

examples.trans: The sweater's size fits you perfectly.
The courtyard is quiet and suitable for work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: منبهات.

examples.trans: Set the alarm for six in the morning.
The alarm rang and we woke up early.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مندهشة, plural: مندهشين).

examples.trans: You look amazed, Madam Suad!
We were all amazed by the coincidence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مناديل.

examples.trans: We arranged the white napkins on the tables.
Here is a clean paper napkin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مناشف.

examples.trans: The room has clean white towels.
Here is a dry towel after the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مناطق.

This area is famous for its stone houses.

examples.trans: He says that while peeking out the window!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

هيك.gloss: like this; so (عشان هيك that's why)

meanings.en: like this; so (عشان هيك that's why)
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine word for 'like this / that way' (عشان هيك 'that is why', مع هيك 'even so').

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
And after that, where do I go?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واسعة, plural: واسعين).

examples.trans: Careful, the pitcher's spout is wide!
The house's courtyard is spacious and sunny.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واصلة, plural: واصلين).

examples.text: ريحة القرفة الدافية واصلة للطابق التاني!
examples.trans: The warm cinnamon scent reaches all the way to the second floor!
The bus is pulling into the station now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واضحة, plural: واضحين).

examples.trans: A sincere, clear sentence from the heart.
The address is clear on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واطية, plural: واطيين).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low wooden beam.
They spoke in a low voice for the guests' sake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أوجاع.

examples.trans: Tiny numbers give me a headache!

examples.text: راح وجع الراس بعد فنجان القهوة.
examples.trans: The headache went away after a cup of coffee.

وجه.gloss: face; top surface (وجه لوجه face to face)

meanings.en: face; top surface (وجه لوجه face to face)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: وجوه.

examples.trans: They stood face to face under the tree.
The top of the cake turned golden in the oven.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of وراء ('behind, past').

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ورد.

examples.trans: We walked past the flower stall.
The scent of roses and jasmine filled the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ورشات.

examples.trans: There is a brass lamp in my workshop downstairs.
The old bag is from my grandfather's workshop.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أوساط.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
The table is right in the middle of the courtyard.

وسع.gloss: to fit; hold; have room for

meanings.en: to fit; hold; have room for
meanings.note: Says how much a place holds: السيارة بتوسع خمس أشخاص 'the car fits five people'. Related to واسع, wide.

examples.trans: The bag doesn't hold all the books.
The table easily fits six.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: وصلات.

examples.trans: Shine the flashlight on the pipe joint.
We tightened the brass fitting with the wrench.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I can hear you clearly on the phone now.
He explained the idea with complete clarity.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: وعود.

examples.trans: We will come next week, promise!
He kept his promise and arrived on time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He greeted the guests with calm dignity.
His speech carries wisdom and poise.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أوقات.

examples.trans: Old pipes take time to warm up.
You arrived right on time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.text: وقفوا كل شي، قديش الساعة هلا؟
examples.trans: Stop everything — what time is it right now?
The driver pulled the car up by the kerb.

meanings.note: With two pronunciations in context: walla ('or' in choice questions: عالشارع ولا عالساحة؟) and wala ('not even / nor': ولا خدش 'not a single scratch', ولا يهمك 'do not worry at all').

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ولاد.

examples.trans: The two boys learned piano together.
May you be blessed, my dear boys.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Takes ب- for the thing promised: وعدته بغرفة 'I promised him a room'.

examples.text: خليني أحزر. وعدت حدا بغرفة مش موجودة عندنا؟
examples.trans: Let me guess. You promised somebody a room we do not have?
I promised you lemon cake on Friday.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: For door handles and bag handles, Jordanian speakers often say يد الباب / عاليد alongside إيد for the human hand.

examples.text: ارفعي يد الباب أول وبعدين ادفعي.
examples.trans: Lift the door handle first, then push.

examples.text: في بطاقة مربوطة على يد الشنتة.
examples.trans: There is a tag tied to the handle of the bag.

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian/Levantine thank-you when someone hands you food, tea, or help (short for يسلموا إيديك 'may your hands be blessed').

examples.trans: Thank you, Salma, for the hot tea!
Thank you, it smells wonderful!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: Ubiquitous Jordanian/Levantine encourager ('come on! / let us...!').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'maybe, perhaps'.

examples.trans: He is maybe thirty-five years old.
Perhaps he got delayed in downtown traffic.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!

meanings.note: Adverb 'on a daily basis, every day'.

examples.trans: The ground floor serves the neighbours daily.
We bake fresh bread daily.
